name: Cylinder head bolts
what: The cylinder head bolts clamp the head and gasket to the engine block.
why: Their specified clamping load helps maintain the combustion seal and prevents coolant or oil leakage at the head joint.
where: They pass through the cylinder head and thread into the engine block at the head-bolt locations.
installationReason: Install the head bolts after the head is seated. Tightening sequence, lubrication, and torque procedure must follow verified service information; values are intentionally not supplied yet.

guide.overview: The ten cylinder head bolts provide the clamping force that holds the head against the block through the head gasket.
guide.operation: The bolts are tightened in a prescribed sequence and in stages to develop an even clamping load across the head. Correct procedure is important because uneven or incorrect clamping can distort components or compromise the gasket seal.
